project.name: memory-system
project.objective: Build a production-grade, tenant-isolated full-stack memory platform for AI agents that durably captures episodes, asynchronously forms provenance-linked versioned memories, exposes API and Python SDK retrieval and bounded context composition, and provides operator inspection, correction, and forgetting controls.

approval.reason: Approved by instruction to proceed to the outline phase.

assumptions.text: PostgreSQL plus pgvector and full-text search can satisfy the first release workload without a dedicated vector or graph database; expected workload remains unverified.
Numeric latency, quality, scale, retention, and availability thresholds can be finalized after expected workload and model providers are selected; those selections remain unresolved.

invariants.text: No operation or retrieval may leak memory across tenants or subjects.
Deleted or suppressed memories must become immediately ineligible for every retrieval and context path.
Memory retrieval or formation failure must not block an agent response; the response path must degrade without personalization.
Every structured memory must retain source evidence and provenance.
Derived inference must never be silently represented as an explicit or observed fact.
Conflicting facts create append-only temporal versions and supersession links rather than destructive overwrites.
Episode persistence and initial formation-job scheduling must be atomic.

decisions.title: First release includes automatic memory formation
decisions.text: Deliver explicit memory operations, bounded retrieval/context composition, episode capture, and asynchronous extraction. Defer knowledge ingestion, graph traversal, decay, consolidation, reflection, and sharing while retaining them as roadmap goals.

decisions.title: Python service and SDK with Next.js console
decisions.text: Use FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Alembic, and Pydantic for the service and first Python SDK, OpenAPI as the transport contract, and Next.js for the operator console. Defer a TypeScript SDK until the API stabilizes.

decisions.title: Explicit tenant subject and actor identities
decisions.text: Carry tenant_id, subject_id, and actor_id at domain boundaries; derive tenant identity from credentials and validate subject and actor membership within the tenant.

decisions.title: Asynchronous capture contract
decisions.text: Episode capture returns durable episode and queryable job identifiers, supports idempotency keys, and documents eventual search visibility. Explicit structured memory addition remains synchronous.

decisions.title: PostgreSQL temporal memory model
decisions.text: Use stable memory identities, append-only versions, validity intervals, supersession links, and many-to-many source evidence in PostgreSQL. Defer arbitrary graph traversal and a graph database.

decisions.title: PostgreSQL-backed initial workflow queue
decisions.text: Use leased PostgreSQL jobs with retries, idempotency, and dead-letter state behind a JobQueue boundary. Preserve atomic episode-and-job creation; if moving to Temporal later, retain atomic capture-to-enqueue through a transactional outbox or equivalent.

decisions.title: Hybrid retrieval and bounded context
decisions.text: Combine PostgreSQL full-text and pgvector candidates, then apply a deterministic versioned ranker over relevance, recency, importance, confidence, and reinforcement. Return cited memories or a token-budgeted context package.

decisions.title: Trust-focused operator console
decisions.text: The first web console supports tenant-scoped search, memory details, source evidence, version history, correction, forgetting, and audit status. Sharing is deferred pending a grant and revocation model.

decisions.title: Production baseline is launch scope
decisions.text: Launch requires tenant isolation, encrypted transport and storage, sensitive-data filtering hooks, immediate suppression, audit events, OpenTelemetry, migration checks, backup/restore verification, and a small golden evaluation set.

knowledge.title: Repository is specification-only
knowledge.text: The repository has no product implementation, package manifest, backend, database migrations, workers, tests, CI, or infrastructure; the runnable HTML is an architecture study only.

knowledge.title: Target system separates online reads from memory formation
knowledge.text: The target architecture independently serves retrieval/context composition and durably captures raw episodes for asynchronous extraction, evaluation, and versioned persistence.
